description:
Title: Interpretable, Explainable and Non-Intrusive Uncertainty Propagation through Expensive-To-Evaluate models via ML-Optimization

Description: Uncertainty models are used in conjunction with a computational model to compute the effects of uncertainties on a system performance.  To support decision making under uncertainties, Uncertainty Quantification methods need to be: 
 
-Interpretable: a human can understand how a prediction was made
-Explainable: the results are presented in a format that is understandable by humans
-Non-intrusive: no modifications of the computational model are carried out and/or no simplifications on the underlying physics are made.
 
Recent advances on the development of two non-intrusive approaches for propagating interval uncertainties through expensive-to-evaluate models exploiting a Machine Learning-based optimization strategy are going to be presented. These two approaches build on Bayesian Optimization to yield an accurate assessment of the performance bounds of an engineering solution, while simultaneously reducing the number of simulations to be evaluated and quantifying the uncertainty in the bounds estimates. 
 
These non-intrusive approaches are interpretable, explainable and yield bounds estimates under-predicting the minimum and over-predicting the true maximum of the performance metric of interest with respect to the current observations available. Indeed, they are advantageous in engineering applications, where a limited number of expensive-to-evaluate models can be investigated.

Bio: Dr. Alice Cicirello (https://sites.google.com/view/dvugroup/people/dr-alice-cicirello) is an Associate Professor at TU Delft. Alice is the founder and the Head of the Data, Vibration and Uncertainty Group (2017), currently leading the MVU laboratory @ TU Delft. Alice joined the Engineering Structures Department @ TU Delft in January 2020. Previous to this position she was a Departmental Lecturer in Dynamics and Vibration at the Oxford Engineering Science Department (Solid Mechanics & Materials Engineering Group) and a Career Development Fellow in Engineering Science at Balliol College (2017-2019). Her research interests span from fundamental to applied research. Her technical expertise covers Uncertainty Quantification and Machine Learning, physics-based modelling, and dynamic experimental testing, and their combination. Alice's research aims at developing effective strategies for supporting decisions in operating conditions and at the design-stage under deep uncertainties. Alice is currently:
 
Head of the Mechanics and Physics of Structure Section at TU Delft Collaborating staff within the Offshore Engineering Section at TU Delft Visiting Fellow at the Engineering Science Department at the University of Oxford (2020 - present) Honorary Lecturer at the Institute for Risk and Uncertainty, Department of Civil Engineering and Industrial Design, University of Liverpool (2017- present) Member of the organising committee of the 10th International Conference on Modern Practice in Stress and Vibration Analysis (MPSVA 2022).
Member of the International Technical Committee of the 8th International Symposium on Reliability Engineering and Risk Management (ISRERM).
